scope: Theorem 1.2 (Finite boundary and polygon estimates) of the manuscript “Cylinder amplitudes and logarithmic bridge-length windows on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Cylinder-amplitudes-and-logarithmic-bridge-length-windows-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 de92d884cd5298c4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are positive constants, independent of the integer parameters, such that BH ≍ H−1/4 , Ag ≍ g−5/4 (H, g ≥ 1). The lower bound for Ag can be restricted to arches of diameter at most Cg, for a fixed sufficiently large C. For every sufficiently large fixed T, bridges of height H whose transverse displacement from the starting normal stays at most TH have mass at least cT H−1/4 and length-weighted mass at most CT H13/12. Either weak sign of terminal transverse displacement may be specified in the mass lower bound. For arches and bridges from a fixed wall port in a strip of height H, the total mass of paths with diameter exceeding r ≥ CH is at most CH−1/4 e−cr/H . Finally, for all sufficiently large R, X R≤diam P<2R µ(P)|P|2 ≤ CR2/3 (1 + log log R).
